exam_set.description: Textbook Practice — Book 1, Chapter 2, Practice Set 2

questions.jp: 図に示す，1桁の2進数xとyを加算して，z（和の1桁目）及びc（桁上げ）を出力する半加算器において，AとBの素子の組合せとして，適切なものはどれか。
questions.romaji: Zu ni shimesu, hitoketa no 2-shinsu x to y o kasan shite, z (wa no hitoketame) oyobi c (ketaage) o shutsuryoku suru hankasanki ni oite, A to B no soshi no kumiawase to shite, tekisetsu na mono wa dore ka.
questions.en: In the half adder shown, one-bit binary values x and y are added and outputs z (the sum bit) and c (the carry) are produced. Which combination of elements A and B is appropriate?

options.label: ア
options.en: A: exclusive OR (XOR); B: logical AND

options.label: イ
options.jp: A：否定論理積，B：否定論理和
options.romaji: A: hitei ronriseki, B: hitei ronriwa

options.label: ウ
options.jp: A：否定論理和，B：排他的論理和
options.romaji: A: hitei ronriwa, B: haitateki ronriwa

options.label: エ
options.en: A: logical AND; B: logical OR

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
A half adder adds two one-bit values. The sum light turns on when exactly one input is 1, while the carry light turns on only when both inputs are 1. Exactly one input is XOR; both inputs are AND.

Technical breakdown:
The half-adder truth table is:

0 + 0 → sum 0, carry 0
0 + 1 → sum 1, carry 0
1 + 0 → sum 1, carry 0
1 + 1 → sum 0, carry 1

Therefore z = x XOR y and c = x AND y. In the diagram, A produces z, so A must be XOR. B produces c, so B must be AND.

Japanese keywords to remember:
半加算器 = hankasanki = half adder
加算 = kasan = addition
和 = wa = sum
桁上げ = ketaage = carry
排他的論理和 = haitateki ronriwa = XOR
論理積 = ronriseki = AND

Why the best solution works:
Option ア assigns XOR to A and AND to B. XOR matches the sum bit for every input pair, and AND matches the carry bit for every input pair.

Wrong answer analysis:
イ — NAND and NOR do not directly produce the half-adder sum and carry truth tables.

ウ — NOR cannot produce the sum bit, and XOR cannot produce a carry only for 1 + 1.

エ — AND as the sum would incorrectly output 1 for 1 + 1, while OR as carry would incorrectly output 1 when only one input is 1.

Memory trick:
Half adder: SUM = XOR, CARRY = AND.

Correct answer: ア

questions.jp: 論理式X＝NOT A・B＋A・NOT B＋NOT A・NOT Bと同じ結果が得られる論理回路はどれか。ここで，論理式中の・は論理積，＋は論理和，NOT AはAの否定を表す。
questions.romaji: Ronrishiki X = NOT A ten B tasu A ten NOT B tasu NOT A ten NOT B to onaji kekka ga erareru ronri kairo wa dore ka. Koko de, ronrishiki-chu no ten wa ronriseki, tasu wa ronriwa, NOT A wa A no hitei o arawasu.
questions.en: Which logic circuit gives the same result as X = (NOT A AND B) OR (A AND NOT B) OR (NOT A AND NOT B)? Here, the dot means AND, plus means OR, and NOT A means the negation of A.

options.label: イ
options.jp: NANDゲート（出力を否定した論理積）
options.romaji: NAND geto (shutsuryoku o hitei shita ronriseki)
options.en: NAND gate: an AND-shaped gate with an output inversion bubble

options.label: エ
options.jp: NORゲート（出力を否定した論理和）
options.romaji: NOR geto (shutsuryoku o hitei shita ronriwa)
options.en: NOR gate: an OR-shaped gate with an output inversion bubble

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Group the two terms that start with NOT A. Whether B is 0 or 1, those terms reduce to NOT A. The remaining expression is true unless both A and B are 1, which is NAND.

Technical breakdown:
Start with:

X = NOT A·B + A·NOT B + NOT A·NOT B

Group the first and third terms:

NOT A·B + NOT A·NOT B
= NOT A(B + NOT B)
= NOT A

Then:

X = NOT A + A·NOT B
= NOT A + NOT B

By De Morgan's law:

NOT A + NOT B = NOT(A·B)

So X is NAND. Visually, NAND is an AND-shaped gate with a small inversion bubble at its output.

Japanese keywords to remember:
論理式 = ronrishiki = Boolean expression
論理積 = ronriseki = AND
論理和 = ronriwa = OR
否定 = hitei = NOT
否定論理積 = hitei ronriseki = NAND
ド・モルガンの法則 = Do Morugan no hosoku = De Morgan's law

Why the best solution works:
Option イ is the NAND symbol. Its output is NOT(A AND B), exactly the simplified expression.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア — AND outputs 1 only when both inputs are 1, the opposite of the required result.

ウ — OR outputs 0 only when both inputs are 0; NAND outputs 0 only when both are 1.

エ — NOR is NOT(A OR B), so it outputs 1 only when both inputs are 0.

Memory trick:
AND gate + output bubble = NAND. OR gate + output bubble = NOR.

Correct answer: イ

questions.jp: 図に示すデジタル回路と等価な論理式はどれか。ここで，論理式中の“・”は論理積を，“＋”は論理和を，NOT XはXの否定を表す。
questions.romaji: Zu ni shimesu dejitaru kairo to toka na ronrishiki wa dore ka. Koko de, ronrishiki-chu no ten wa ronriseki o, tasu wa ronriwa o, NOT X wa X no hitei o arawasu.
questions.en: Which Boolean expression is equivalent to the digital circuit shown? In the expressions, the dot means AND, plus means OR, and NOT X means the negation of X.

options.label: ア
options.romaji: X = A AND B OR A AND NOT B
options.en: X = (A AND B) OR (A AND NOT B)

options.label: イ
options.romaji: X = A AND B OR NOT A AND NOT B
options.en: X = (A AND B) OR (NOT A AND NOT B)

options.label: ウ
options.romaji: X = A AND NOT B OR NOT A AND B
options.en: X = (A AND NOT B) OR (NOT A AND B)

options.label: エ
options.romaji: X = (NOT A OR B) AND (A OR NOT B)
options.en: X = (NOT A OR B) AND (A OR NOT B)

questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Follow the wires from left to right. A and B are first flipped. Their flipped values are ORed, and that shared result is combined once with A and once with B. The final OR keeps the cases where A and B differ.

Technical breakdown:
The NOT gates produce NOT A and NOT B. The first OR produces:

NOT A + NOT B

The upper AND branch is:

A(NOT A + NOT B)

The lower branch is:

B(NOT A + NOT B)

The final OR gives:

X = A(NOT A + NOT B) + B(NOT A + NOT B)

Expanding:

X = A·NOT A + A·NOT B + B·NOT A + B·NOT B

Because A·NOT A = 0 and B·NOT B = 0:

X = A·NOT B + NOT A·B

This is XOR.

Japanese keywords to remember:
デジタル回路 = dejitaru kairo = digital circuit
等価 = toka = equivalent
論理式 = ronrishiki = Boolean expression
論理積 = ronriseki = AND
論理和 = ronriwa = OR
否定 = hitei = NOT
排他的論理和 = haitateki ronriwa = XOR

Why the best solution works:
Option ウ is 1 precisely for A=1, B=0 or A=0, B=1, matching the traced circuit and XOR truth table.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア — This simplifies to A, so it ignores the cases required when only B is 1.

イ — This is XNOR: it is 1 when A and B are equal, opposite to XOR.

エ — This also represents equality/XNOR, not the unequal-input behavior of the circuit.

Memory trick:
Trace gates in order: NOT → OR → two AND branches → final OR. Then simplify complements such as A·NOT A to 0.

Correct answer: ウ

questions.jp: 図は全加算器を表す論理回路である。図中のxに1，yに0，zに1を入力したとき，出力となるc（けた上げ数），s（和）の値はどれか。
questions.romaji: Zu wa zenkasanki o arawasu ronri kairo de aru. Zuchu no x ni 1, y ni 0, z ni 1 o nyuryoku shita toki, shutsuryoku to naru c (ketaage-su), s (wa) no atai wa dore ka.
questions.en: The diagram is a full-adder circuit. When x=1, y=0, and z=1 are input, which values are output as c (carry) and s (sum)?
questions.explanation:
ELI5:
Add the three input bits: 1 + 0 + 1 = binary 10. The right digit is the sum bit 0, and the left digit is the carry 1.

Technical breakdown:
A full adder accepts two data bits plus a carry-in. Its sum is the XOR of all three inputs:

s = 1 XOR 0 XOR 1 = 0

The carry becomes 1 when at least two inputs are 1. Here x and z are both 1, so:

c = 1

Thus the output pair is c=1, s=0. A half adder has only two input bits; a full adder includes the third carry-in bit.

Japanese keywords to remember:
全加算器 = zenkasanki = full adder
入力 = nyuryoku = input
出力 = shutsuryoku = output
けた上げ数 = ketaage-su = carry value
和 = wa = sum

Why the best solution works:
Option ウ gives c=1 and s=0, which is the two-bit binary result 10 from adding 1+0+1.

Wrong answer analysis:
ア — It loses the carry produced by the two input 1s.

イ — It gives binary 01, equal to decimal 1 rather than the required decimal 2.

エ — It gives binary 11, equal to decimal 3; only two of the three inputs are 1.

Memory trick:
Count the 1s: 0 or 1 ones gives carry 0; 2 or 3 ones gives carry 1. The sum bit is 1 for an odd number of ones and 0 for an even number.

Correct answer: ウ
